blocks.title: Honors — one structure, not two units
blocks.markdown: Today the force tools come together. The honors move is to see that **kinematics and forces are not two separate subjects** — they're the front and back of a single machine. Force decides acceleration; acceleration decides how the motion unfolds. Connect the arc out loud.

## Connect the arc — forces and kinematics are one structure

Trace the chain you've built since Day 1:

1. **Kinematics** gave you the language of *how* things move: position, velocity, acceleration — and the equations that link them.
2. **Newton's laws** answered the *why*: $\Sigma\vec{F} = m\vec{a}$ says the net force **sets** the acceleration.
3. A **free-body diagram** is the bridge: it turns a physical situation into the one number — net force — that feeds $a = \Sigma F / m$.

So the structure runs **one direction**: *forces → net force → acceleration → (back into kinematics) → the whole future motion.* Friction, the normal force, weight, tension — every contact force you've studied is just an input to that single pipeline. There was never a 'kinematics chapter' and a 'forces chapter.' There's one chain, and today you can finally see both ends of it at once. That is what it means to **own** Unit 1 rather than to have covered it.

blocks.frame: Forces connect to kinematics through ___. If I knew every force on the asteroid, the step that turns that into its future position is ___, because ___.
blocks.prompt: JUSTIFY: Explain, as a single connected chain, how a free-body diagram leads all the way to a prediction of an object's future position. Name each link (net force → acceleration → motion) and defend why you can't skip the middle step.
